Silicone is not an oil compound

It has the widest temperature range of the three and the weakest abrasion resistance, and it swells in hot mineral oil. If your pump handles oil, specify NBR or FKM — saying so is cheaper than a failed inlay.

What is the minimum order quantity for this part?

We supply in bulk. The minimum run is 10,000 pieces per part number, per compound — and because silicone, FKM and NBR shrink differently, each compound needs its own tool. Prototype and first-article lots sit outside the minimum.
Can you match a competitor specification or reverse-engineer an existing part?

Yes. Send the worn inlay and tell us what the pump handles and how hot it runs — a used insert has taken a compression set and measures thinner than moulded, so we work to the housing and the free thickness, not to the sample.
What file formats do you accept for drawings?
PDF, DWG, DXF and STEP. Mark the housing bore, the free thickness and the working compression — and state the medium and temperature, which decide the compound before any dimension matters.
Do you provide material test reports with each shipment?

Yes. Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Hardness, tensile to ASTM D412 and compression set to ASTM D395 Method B are tested in-house. We do not hold food-contact or pharmaceutical approvals — tell us which scheme you need and we will confirm what we can supply.
What are your payment and delivery terms for international orders?
TT and LC accepted, discussed per order. Ex-works Nashik or FOB Nhava Sheva. Commercial invoice, packing list and certificate of origin are issued with every consignment.
